text.p: The following are leading domestic stories in Portuguese newspapers.
- Demand in the flotation of mobile phone operator Telecel is weak. Sources close to the process say the share price, between 6,900 and 8,100 escudos, is considered to be high.

- Two senior officers of Portugues do Atlantico (BPA) have been found innocent in the U.S. of accusations of money laundering due to insufficient evidence, according to a document made available to the paper.
- The Portuguese government will have prepared a restructuring plan for ship repairer Lisnave by December 16, sources involved in the process told the paper.

- Rightwing Popular Party (PP) leader Manuel Monteiro will meet Socialist Prime Minister Antonio Guterres today to explain why the PP will abstain in the vote in parliament on the 1997 budget on December 11.
- Sonae president Belmiro de Azevedo believes the group's business in Brazil will grow substantially in the coming years.
- At a conference in Oporto, Sonae challenged Banco Portugues de Investimento (BPI) to establish itself in Brazil.
